requirements.req_text: Emergency Situations. Do the following: (a) Discuss with your counselor the aspects of emergency preparedness and include in your discussion the kinds of questions that are important to ask yourself as you consider each of these: prevention, protection, mitigation, response, and recovery. (b) Using a chart, spreadsheet, or another method approved by your counselor, demonstrate your understanding of each aspect of emergency preparedness listed in requirement 1(a) (prevention, protection, mitigation, response, and recovery) for 10 emergency situations from the list below. Discuss your findings with your counselor. (1) Home stovetop or oven fire (2) Home flammable liquid fire (3) Gas leak in or near a home or with outside cooking (4) Food poisoning (5) Automobile crash (6) Vehicle stalled in the desert (7) Vehicle trapped in a blizzard (8) Backcountry injury (9) Boating or water accident (10) Toxic chemical spills and releases (11) Nuclear power plant emergency (12) Fire or explosion in a public place (13) Violence in a public place (14) Wildland fire (15) Avalanche (snowslide or rockslide) (16) Earthquake (17) Tsunami (18) Major flooding or a flash flood with water outage (19) Hurricane with power outage (20) Tornado (21) Lightning storm

pamphlet_excerpts: Airway Priority: Clearing blocked breathing passages always precedes treatment of secondary extremity fractures.
Hemorrhage Control: Direct pressure and arterial tourniquets stop catastrophic life-threatening blood loss quickly.
Shock Management: Elevating legs and conserving body heat preserves vital organ perfusion effectively.
Triage Classification: Sorting casualties by injury severity ensures optimal allocation of medical resources.

Step 4 - Transport Preparation: Stabilize fractures with padded rigid splints before moving casualties toward ambulances.

requirements.description: Careers. Do ONE of the following: (a) Interview an emergency services coordinator or a civil servant about their work in disaster management. Learn about how they chose this career and about their duties. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career. (b) Identify three career opportunities that would use skills and knowledge in emergency services. Pick one and research the training, education, certification requirements, experience, and expenses associated with entering the field. Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities, and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career. (c) Identify how you might use the skills and knowledge in the field of emergency preparedness to pursue a personal hobby and/or healthy lifestyle. Research the additional training required, expenses, and affiliation with organizations that would help you maximize the enjoyment and benefit you might gain from it. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and share what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Emergency Preparedness Requirement 1, emergency management is organized around five mission areas: Prevention, Protection, Mitigation, Response, and Recovery. Which action is an example of Mitigation before a disaster strikes?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Emergency Preparedness Requirement 1, emergency management is organized around five mission areas: Prevention, Protection, Mitigation, Response, and Recovery. Which action is an example of Mitigation before a disaster strikes?
options: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, elevating utilities above flood level.
B. Dispatching search-and-rescue helicopters during the peak of a hurricane to pull stranded residents from rooftops.
C. Applying for long-term federal rebuilding loans six months after a tornado destroys a town business district.
D. Waiting until a wildfire evacuation order is issued to start looking for flashlights, water bottles, and family phone numbers.
choices: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, elevating utilities above flood level.
B. Dispatching search-and-rescue helicopters during the peak of a hurricane to pull stranded residents from rooftops.
C. Applying for long-term federal rebuilding loans six months after a tornado destroys a town business district.
D. Waiting until a wildfire evacuation order is issued to start looking for flashlights, water bottles, and family phone numbers.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, elevating utilities above flood level, or clearing defensible brush space around a home to reduce future disaster damage.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Mitigation consists of sustained actions taken before an emergency (such as seismic bracing, flood elevation, and fuel reduction) that eliminate or reduce the long-term risk and severity of loss of life and property.

B. Test alarms once a month and replace batteries once a year

D. Test alarms weekly and replace batteries only when they chirp
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Test alarms once a month and replace batteries once a year
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Smoke alarms should be tested once a month, and their batteries should be replaced once a year to ensure reliable operation during a fire (p. 26).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In emergency preparedness, how do automatic sprinkler systems in schools and smoke alarms in homes function when a fire breaks out?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In emergency preparedness, how do automatic sprinkler systems in schools and smoke alarms in homes function when a fire breaks out?
options: A. They act as prevention measures by stopping electrical sparks from igniting
B. They serve as mitigation measures by limiting fire spread and helping occupants escape alive
C. They replace the need for a preplanned family escape route
D. They represent the recovery phase of disaster management
choices: A. They act as prevention measures by stopping electrical sparks from igniting
B. They serve as mitigation measures by limiting fire spread and helping occupants escape alive
C. They replace the need for a preplanned family escape route
D. They represent the recovery phase of disaster management
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. They serve as mitigation measures by limiting fire spread and helping occupants escape alive
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Smoke alarms, escape routes, and automatic sprinkler systems mitigate an emergency by keeping the fire from spreading and ensuring occupants get out alive, making the outcome less severe (p. 19).

options: A. Rush in immediately before the situation gets worse
B. Keep yourself safe first and never put yourself in danger of becoming a second victim
C. Always attempt a swimming rescue before looking for reaching or throwing gear
D. Wait to locate building exits only after an alarm sounds
choices: A. Rush in immediately before the situation gets worse
B. Keep yourself safe first and never put yourself in danger of becoming a second victim
C. Always attempt a swimming rescue before looking for reaching or throwing gear
D. Wait to locate building exits only after an alarm sounds
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Keep yourself safe first and never put yourself in danger of becoming a second victim
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Before attempting any rescue, you must assess the hazard and ensure you do not put yourself in danger, recognizing that sometimes the safest action is to stay clear and call professionals (p. 71).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does a rescue aircraft pilot signal to people on the ground that their message has NOT been understood?
options: A. By dipping the nose of the airplane up and down
B. By rocking the wings from side to side or flashing green lights
C. By making a complete right-hand circle or flashing red lights
D. By fishtailing or zigzagging the aircraft across the sky
choices: A. By dipping the nose of the airplane up and down
B. By rocking the wings from side to side or flashing green lights
C. By making a complete right-hand circle or flashing red lights
D. By fishtailing or zigzagging the aircraft across the sky
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. By making a complete right-hand circle or flashing red lights
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): If a pilot does not understand your ground signal, the aircraft will fly a complete right-hand circle or flash red lights, while wing-rocking or green lights mean the message was understood (p. 40).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When just you and a buddy are transporting an injured person out of a remote area, what rest schedule does the Emergency Preparedness pamphlet recommend?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When just you and a buddy are transporting an injured person out of a remote area, what rest schedule does the Emergency Preparedness pamphlet recommend?
options: A. Hike continuously without stopping until reaching a paved road
B. Stop every 10 minutes and rest for 20 minutes
C. Stop every 30 to 60 minutes and rest for 5 to 10 minutes
D. Stop only once every three hours for water
choices: A. Hike continuously without stopping until reaching a paved road
B. Stop every 10 minutes and rest for 20 minutes
C. Stop every 30 to 60 minutes and rest for 5 to 10 minutes
D. Stop only once every three hours for water
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Stop every 30 to 60 minutes and rest for 5 to 10 minutes
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): To conserve energy and avoid becoming a second casualty, two rescuers transporting a victim should stop every 30 to 60 minutes and rest for 5 to 10 minutes, adjusting for weight and terrain (p. 55).
